builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas
summary: The method replaces single-idea quality optimization and prompt-based diversity heuristics with set-level reinforcement learning, in which K jointly generated idea cards are scored with each idea's quality weighted by its distance from its predecessors. It costs an RL training pipeline with a joint set-scoring reward function, plus the evaluation infrastructure needed to measure pairwise idea distance, none of which is feasible on a single 24 GB GPU or a limited API budget. It can fail if the distance metric rewards superficial variation rather than genuine conceptual novelty, and the human evidence is a pilot study with only four experts, so quality and executability claims remain preliminary.
rationale: The contribution depends on RL training with a custom set-level reward, which the reader's infrastructure cannot support, though the distance-weighted set scoring idea could later inform prompt-time diversification with API models.
technique: Set-level RL for diverse grounded ideation

It costs an RL training pipeline with a joint set-scoring reward function, plus the evaluation infrastructure needed to measure pairwise idea distance, none of which is feasible on a single 24 GB GPU or a limited API budget. It can fail if the distance metric rewards superficial variation rather than genuine conceptual novelty, and the human evidence is a pilot study with only four experts, so quality and executability claims remain preliminary.

A trained 8B model achieves higher creative utility (combined quality-diversity) than Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-6 Astra on a contamination-free benchmark, with comparable expert ratings and success@k on executed proof-of-concept experiments.
